sections.name: architecture
sections.value: Rust only. u1: Omp|Pi route directly to the queue-backed Observe/message.pushed stream before Transport, composer gates, and select_rung. u2 (ruling 2026-09-02): the actual drain is crates/daemon/src/pointer/worker.rs; add config thresholds, a dedicated per-sender queued-notice queue, additive /v1/notices read-and-ack in daemon/http, and cli/client + main stderr rendering. Notices never enter or compete with the user inbox; no envelope version bump. u3: pane tap bytes are rendered output, never keystrokes; a fresh recognized composer box is authoritative. Blank permits; non-blank returns human-typing with the first 12 hex of SHA-256 in additive draft_sha fields on InjectionVerdict, StagedSubmission, and DeliveryOutcome::Queued.

value.rationale: u1 is ~20 lines and urgent — ship it in the first commit; u2 follows on the same branch

value.name: omp/pi bypass the composer veto

value.name: sender notices

value.note: Prime ruling 2026-09-02 approved the widened actual drain + /v1/notices/client wiring. Dedicated notice kind only; per-sender read-and-ack; body names msg_id, recipient, reason, attempts, age; additive, no envelope bump. AC7 caps retry interval at a configured default no greater than 30 seconds.

value.name: claude veto = composer box only
value.paths: crates/harnesses/src/interaction.rs (permits_with_additional_veto / observe_composer_at — find what other than the composer box feeds the veto: tap-activity recency? output bytes?), crates/harnesses/src/composer.rs, tests
value.test_strategy: RED-first with a fake tap that streams agent OUTPUT bytes while the composer box is blank; assert permitted
value.note: hypothesis: record_tap on any drained tap bytes marks the pane as recently-typed; agent output through the tap looks like keystrokes. Verify before fixing.

Default: each coder gets its own worktree, branching off the PM's plan branch; unit lands back onto the plan branch (PM merges — coders never merge). Shared-tree work is the retro-proven #1 hazard (staged sweeps, untrustworthy greens) — only choose it for trivially disjoint single-wave work, and then file-scoped `git add` only, never -A. REMEMBER: fences partition WRITE intent, not the build — a mid-refactor sibling can still break your compile, so waves must respect build dependencies, and a broken workspace build is a PM composition concern, not a coder's to fix cross-fence.

value.steps: u1 commit + live proof FIRST (so it can ship alone if u2 slips); u2; cargo receipts; harness checks; PR

value.when: after composition (or after solo-pm coding), before the PR into main
value.inputs: plan.dd.md + this impl-guide + full branch diff; priority = plan promises, composition seams, interface drift, correctness, contract-test gaps

value.text: Keep to the named paths; ask prime before widening.
